results.summary: The particle distribution is reproduced exactly. A seed always gives the same particle arrays, bit for bit: across reloads, when re-sampled in place, at both tiers, and in 4 JavaScript engines (Chromium V8, Node V8, Bun JSC, and the WebKitGTK 2.52.6 jsc shell that the Tauri shell uses). All 7 seeds tested give identical digests everywhere (default seed 20260919: medium d1c97a08, low e9d5d30f). A different seed changes 36 000 of 36 000 home coordinates. Rebuilding the right hand from pose-right.json gives a byte-identical GLB (sha256 cd212569…) and contour file (76b9d15f…). No Math.random or Date is on the sampling or render path. On one device, a frozen-clock frame is also identical pixel for pixel: 0 px differ across reloads on SwiftShader and on an Intel Iris Xe GPU, at both tiers, after 6 resamples, and for scrubbed startup frames at p 0.25/0.5/0.75. Across GPUs the rendered frame is not the same. The shader computes breathing phase, gather lead and pointer factor with fract(sin(aId*127.1)*43758.5453), and that result depends on the GPU. With the same seed, Xe and SwiftShader agree on only about 1.5 % of these per-particle values. In the particle region the Xe and SwiftShader frames differ in 32 903 px (>32 levels), against 41 780 px between two different seeds on the same GPU. The left hand differs in only 429 px (>8). So "same seed rebuilds the same frame" (rng.ts header, DECISIONS.md:47) holds only per device, and the A2 test checks only the arrays in SwiftShader. A2 passes today (1/1, 13.2 s).

findings.title: The same seed renders a different dot arrangement on a different GPU (fract(sin) hash in the particle shader)
findings.description: The shader computes its per-particle constants in the vertex shader: breathing phase h2, gather lead h1 and pointer factor h3, each as fract(sin(n*127.1)*43758.5453). With n up to about 12 000, the argument reaches about 1.5e6. At that size the result depends on the GPU's sin precision. SwiftShader and Intel Xe agree for only about 1.5 % of ids, and neither matches exact f32 math. At the home view the clock is 0 but the drift is not, so each dot moves a GPU-dependent amount (predicted hand median 1.9 px, max 5.5; tail up to 17.5 px). Measured in the particle region, Xe vs SwiftShader with the same seed differ in 32 903 px (>32 levels). Seed 1 vs the default seed on the same GPU differ in 41 780 px. So the same seed on another GPU looks about 79 % as different as another seed, while the left hand differs only by raster noise (429 px >8). The hand shape is kept; the individual dots are not. rng.ts:1-5 and DECISIONS.md:47 claim that 'a given seed always rebuilds the same frame' (for spec 7.3 reversible transitions and stable screenshots), and the shader comment says hashing 'can reproduce them exactly'. That holds per device only. The A2 test proves only the CPU arrays, in SwiftShader. rng.ts already has an integer hash11 meant for exactly this job, but nothing uses it. Consequence: SwiftShader captures (including the D10 evidence) will not match the user's desktop dot for dot. No decision in D1-D26 covers this.

findings.title: A2 test and digest prove less than 'the same frame'
findings.description: A2 hashes the six CPU arrays at the medium tier and the default seed, in one engine (SwiftShader Chromium). The following are not in the suite: the low tier, the aScatter attribute (derived), frozen-frame pixel identity, other GPUs, and the WebKitGTK webview. Those were checked by hand in this review: low tier, scatter hashes, and frames per device all match. What the test claims ('same cloud, bit for bit, across a reload and in place') is true. The docs that describe it (CONTRACTS §9, log-v2 A2 'Fixed and verified') should not be read as frame reproducibility.

findings.title: Breathing hash has only a few hundred distinct phases
findings.description: Because of the same sin precision loss, h2 takes only 424 distinct values over 12 000 ids on SwiftShader (537 on Xe). Particles therefore breathe in lockstep groups of about 28 rather than each with its own phase. This is not visible in stills. It may show as clumped co-motion in motion, which the user's desktop run in step 7 would reveal.

findings.title: Scrubbed or reversed startup frames depend on how long the scene idled
findings.description: stage.idleTime keeps counting while the stage is 'home' and is not reset when the stage goes back to 'intro'. The shader's breathing phase uTime = idleTime/period is therefore carried into the gather. With timeScale 0, scrubStartup(p) on fresh loads is pixel-identical. After 3 s of idle, the same p differs by 42 372 px (p 0.5) and 49 294 px (p 0.75), in the particle hand only. The reverse transition (spec 7.3) is not built yet, so this is only a heads-up for it. Review A2 itself says a return-animation failure cannot be inferred.

findings.title: Dev ?seed values of 2^32 or more alias smaller seeds
findings.description: particleSeed accepts any digit string, but makeRng applies seed>>>0. So ?seed=4294967296 samples the same cloud as seed 0, while particleDigest.seed reports 4294967296. This is dev and test only; the product always uses SCENE_SEED.

decisionsForUser: seed-1: Should the per-particle constants be the same on every GPU? Option (a): replace the shader's fract(sin()) with a GPU-portable integer hash. That could be rng.ts's unused hash11, precomputed into an attribute, or a uint hash in GLSL ES 3.0. The home-view dot arrangement would change once, and D10's particle_shape baseline would need re-measuring. Option (b): accept per-device reproducibility and change the claims in rng.ts and DECISIONS.md:47 (and the shader comment) to 'same frame on the same device'. No existing decision (D1-D26) covers this.

seed-4: When the reverse transition is built, should idleTime/uTime be reset or eased to 0 on leaving home, so that the return frames depend only on the seed and the progress? Or should the breathing phase carry over by design?

At the home view the product has no visible seams in the sense review A used ("tubular stitching", white triangle gaps at the wrist and finger roots). Both GLBs are one welded shell. In the browser (__alpha.handMesh): 14 429 vertices and 28 854 triangles per hand, all positions unique, 0 boundary edges, 0 non-manifold edges, 0 duplicated directed edges, and 0 split normals, so there are no hard-normal shading seams. These numbers match the builder mesh reports (glb_check: winding 1.0, a1.pass true, final minimum triangle angle p1 30.1 deg). results.reason:
The finding reproduces in full, and the cause is the one the reviewer names. No decision in D1-D26 covers it, and it belongs under "does the same seed reproduce?". I checked this myself: with breathing drift switched off, SwiftShader and Xe differ only by raster noise. So the fract(sin) hash is what makes the same seed give a different frame on a different GPU. Seed reproduction still holds for the CPU arrays (the digests match on both GPUs) and for frames on one device (0 px difference between loads). It fails only across GPUs.

I would lower the severity from major to minor, for two reasons:
(1) A viewer at the home view cannot notice it. Each device shows one consistent, breathing arrangement, and in normal use uTime advances, so the dots never hold a fixed layout anyway.
(2) No check claims more than it proves. The A2 test and CONTRACTS §9 claim only the cloud arrays (the "cloud hash"), and that is proven on both GPUs. The overstatements are in comments and docs: rng.ts:1-5 and DECISIONS.md:47 say "same frame", and the shader comment says "reproduce them exactly".

One consequence the reviewer did not quantify: the hash moves the D10 metrics between devices. On Xe the default-seed negative-space score falls to 0.659, against a gate of 0.65. That matters for step 7, because SwiftShader's D10 margins do not carry over to the user's desktop. It is a question for the user, not a failed gate: the D10 gate still passed on Xe here, and it already samples an arbitrary breathing phase on a single GPU. For the user: should reproducibility mean the same frame on every GPU (switch the shader to the integer hash11, or pass per-particle phases as attributes), or only on the same device? If the second, the docs and comments should be scoped down.
results.evidence:
All files are under /home/a/Documents/Alpha/outputs/qa/scratch/review6/verify-seed-1/. The scripts are gh.mjs, cap.mjs and capr.mjs (capr.mjs is cap.mjs with reducedMotion). I did not run the Playwright suite; the only thing written in the repo is this scratch directory.

1. Hash readback (gh.mjs → ss.json, xe.json). The shader's hash(aId), hash(aId+19.7) and hash(aId+51.3) were read back for 12 000 ids on two renderers: SwiftShader, and ANGLE Vulkan on Intel Iris Xe RPL-P (Mesa).
   - Share of ids where the two agree: h1 1.52 %, h2 1.46 %, h3 1.35 %.
   - Median circular difference: about 0.25, i.e. the two are uncorrelated.
   - Distinct values: SwiftShader 410/424/407, Xe 546/537/539.
   - These match the reviewer's stats.json.

2. Frozen home frames (cap.mjs; setTimeScale(0) before home; idleTime 0; digest d1c97a08 on both GPUs). Pixel counts that differ, left hand = x<800 at >8 levels, particle region = x≥800 at >32 levels:

   | Comparison | Left hand | Particle region |
   |---|---|---|
   | Same GPU, two loads (SS or Xe) | 0 | 0 |
   | SS vs Xe, same default seed | 541 | 32 903 |
   | SS, default vs seed 1 | 0 | 41 780 |
   | Xe, default vs seed 1 | 0 | 40 146 |
   | SS, seed 1 vs seed 2 | 0 | 41 774 |

   Crop: crop-ss-xe-seed1.png (SS | Xe | seed 1; crop 880,440-1180,640 at 2x). It shows a different dot arrangement with the same hand shape.

3. Isolating the cause (capr.mjs, reducedMotion 'reduce', so breathAmplitude is 0 per src/config/timing.ts:51). With the drift off, SS vs Xe differ in 2 621 px in the particle region, against 38 389 px for seed 1. So about 92 % of the cross-GPU difference comes from the hash-driven drift.

4. D10 gate (scripts/particle_shape.py on each frame; output in ps-*/particle-shape.json):

   | Frame | IoU | Contour mean | Negative space | Gate |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | SS default | 0.898 | 4.90 px | 0.755 | pass |
   | Xe default | 0.866 | 6.24 px | 0.659 (gate ≥ 0.65) | pass |
   | SS seed 1 | – | – | – | fails (pinky tip 11.18 px) |
   | Xe seed 1 | – | – | – | pass |
   | Reduced motion, SS | 0.8776 | 5.95 px | 0.6966 | pass |
   | Reduced motion, Xe | 0.8763 | 5.99 px | 0.6959 | pass |

   With the drift off the two GPUs score almost the same; with it on they move apart.

5. Scope of the claims. tests/acceptance.spec.ts:5 and :116-131 and docs/CONTRACTS.md:290-294 claim only the cloud arrays and their digest. The "same frame" wording is only in src/hand/rng.ts:1-5, docs/DECISIONS.md:47, and the shader comment at src/scene/ParticleHand.tsx:160-162. The hash is at ParticleHand.tsx:162, the drift at :174-178, and src/hand/rng.ts:24-28 (hash11) is not used anywhere. None of the "SwiftShader / GPU" caveats in log-v2 or ACCEPTANCE mention this, so it is not a known issue.
